explain.say: A car wheel is held on by just five bolts, yet it carries a tonne of car round corners. The secret is preload: the bolts are tightened until they stretch like stiff springs and squeeze the parts together. Look at the reasons on the board.

draw.text: Preload: the tension put into a bolt when it is tightened

explain.say: Take an M12 bolt of grade 8.8. Its proof load, the most it can take without permanent stretch, is about 49 kilonewtons. Designers often preload to 75 percent of that: about 36.7 kilonewtons. The wrench torque is roughly 0.2 times preload times diameter: about 88 newton metres. Why not tighten it to the limit?

explain.say: You need some margin for the working load. Now the clever part. When an external load P pulls the joint apart, the bolt and the clamped plates share it according to their stiffness. Plates are usually much stiffer, so the bolt feels only a fraction C, here 25 percent. See the gently rising line? That is the bolt.

explain.say: The other 75 percent just reduces the clamp force between the plates. See the falling line? At 10 kilonewtons of load, the clamp drops from 36.7 to 29.2 kilonewtons, while the bolt only rises by 2.5. The joint stays shut until the clamp reaches zero. At what load does that happen?

explain.say: At 36.7 over 0.75, about 49 kilonewtons: where the line crosses zero. Then the bolt takes everything and the joint gapes. Great work! Real link: wind turbine tower bolts are tightened with hydraulic tensioners and checked regularly. Exam tip: the bolt sees only C times any fluctuating load, which is why preload helps fatigue.

faq.q: Why tighten a bolt so hard?
faq.a: Preload clamps the parts together so the joint is stiff, the bolt sees only a small part of any extra load, fatigue stress swings are small, and friction resists loosening.
asks: why are bolts tightened to a preload

faq.q: How much of an external load does a bolt feel?
faq.a: Only a fraction C, the joint stiffness constant, which is the bolt stiffness divided by bolt plus member stiffness. Often C is around 0.2 to 0.3.

faq.q: What happens to the clamp force when the joint is loaded?
faq.a: It falls by 1 minus C times the external load. When it reaches zero the plates separate and the bolt carries the whole load.

faq.q: How do I find bolt tightening torque?
faq.a: A common estimate is T equals K times F i times d, with the nut factor K about 0.2 for dry steel threads.

faq.q: What is the proof load of a bolt?
faq.a: The largest tension a bolt can carry without permanent stretch: proof strength times tensile stress area. For an M12 grade 8.8 bolt it is about 49 kilonewtons.

facts: An M12 coarse thread has a tensile stress area of about 84.3 mm².
Bolts are commonly preloaded to about 75 % of proof load for reusable joints.

quiz.say: A bolt has a preload of 20 kilonewtons and a joint constant C of 0.2. An external load of 10 kilonewtons is applied. What is the bolt tension?
quiz.show: Preload 20 kN, C = 0.2, external load 10 kN. Bolt tension?

wrong.1: That assumes the bolt takes the whole external load; the stiff plates take most of it.
wrong.2: That is the clamp force, 20 − 0.8 × 10, not the bolt tension.
